version.changelog:
web-browser v0.2.8

- Documentation files updated for improved clarity and detail in SKILL.md and CHANGELOG.md.
- Removed skill-card.md file.
- No changes to core logic or functional behavior.

llm.summary: The skill is a browser automation helper, but its credential workflow pushes agents to collect, persist, and reuse sensitive secrets with too little scoping or consent.

dimensions.detail: The skill directs use of real browser sessions, closed shadow DOM inspection, local credential stores, .env files, project memory, Vault, GitHub secrets, and raw CDP where available; those powers are relevant to the purpose but broader than safely scoped by default.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill instructs runtime installation/execution of mutable Playwright packages using @latest, so reviewed behavior can change after installation. No malicious dependency is present in the artifact itself.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions use broad triggers such as browser test, open login screen, issue token, and service credential, then contain hard stops that discourage manual alternatives and make backend automation mandatory for sensitive credential steps.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no backdoor or OS service persistence, but the credential workflow requires durable secret persistence in keyrings, Vault, .env files, skill data, or provider secret stores before handoff, which materially increases blast radius.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The UI-testing and browser-routing purpose is coherent, but the credential-issue topic goes beyond ordinary browser assistance by requiring token issuance, token extraction from pages, persistence, and downstream automation when API credentials are missing.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you explicitly want an agent to help with authenticated browser workflows and credential issuance. Before use, require exact service/account/scope/destination approval, avoid plaintext command-line secrets, pin runtime dependencies, keep TLS validation enabled for credential entry, and do not allow broad .env/Vault/memory scans or mandatory persistence unless you chose the storage target.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: Downgraded: scripts/cdp-trace.js is only an auxiliary CDP trace script; the package also includes SKILL.md, ui-test.md, and credential-issue.md, which do document the broader declared workflows.
[AE1] unexpected: Overridden: the referenced cdp-trace.md and credential-issue.md files were present locally and fully inspected during this review.
[SSD-3] expected: Credential handling is declared, but the artifact-backed instructions make collection, programmatic extraction, persistence, and handoff of newly issued secrets mandatory, which is a material Review concern.
[PE3] expected: Use of credential stores is expected for this purpose, but the workflow normalizes access to reusable local and cloud credentials including Docker, AWS, Vault, GitHub, and provider tokens.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Accepted as a scoping concern: broad activation phrases can route ordinary browser/login requests into sensitive credential workflows without a narrow intent gate.
[SQP-2] expected: Accepted in context: the skill discloses credential workflows, but it lacks a strong per-action consent model before session reuse, secret-store inspection, token extraction, and persistence.
[EA2] expected: Partially accepted: some cited login-wall examples actually tell the agent to ask the user, but the credential workflow still over-forces backend automation after login and before user copy fallback.
[E5] expected: Downgraded: aws s3 cp/R2 upload is disclosed as a handoff and PR image-hosting scenario, not hidden exfiltration; users should still verify destination ownership.
[TM1] expected: Downgraded: the Tailscale DELETE endpoint is part of a disclosed revoke flow with identifier checks, not by itself evidence of tool-parameter abuse.
[T05] expected: Accepted: mandatory broad discovery of stored credentials and mandatory durable persistence exceed least-privilege needs even though credential issuance is a declared feature.
[T09] unexpected: Accepted: --login user:pass plus ignoreHTTPSErrors: true in cdp-trace.js, and example commands embedding tokens in shell arguments, create avoidable credential-exposure risks.
[T08] unexpected: Accepted: @playwright/mcp@latest and playwright@latest are mutable runtime dependencies and are not pinned to reviewed versions.
